answers: Calico enforces policies through a network plug-in that is integrated with every IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service cluster. It achieves this by implementing Iptables rules, which function as a firewall for the worker node. These rules define the criteria that network traffic must meet in order to be forwarded to the intended resource, including any Kubernetes network policies.

history.content: What is the difference between Calico policy Description and Kubernetes policy Description?

The Calico policy Description refers to the policies that are specific to the Calico network plugin in a Kubernetes cluster. These policies are used to manage and control network traffic in the cluster, allowing or blocking traffic based on network interfaces, pod sources or destinations, and Kubernetes services.
On the other hand, Kubernetes policy Description refers to the policies that are built into Kubernetes and limit access to the Kubernetes Dashboard. These policies are applied at the pod level and affect all classic and VPC clusters. They are used to block all pods from accessing the Kubernetes Dashboard or the dashboard metrics scraper, unless the pod is deployed in a namespace that has the appropriate labels.
In summary, Calico policies are focused on managing and controlling network traffic, while Kubernetes policies are focused on limiting access to the Kubernetes Dashboard.

Kubernetes network policies
: [Kubernetes network policies](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/) specify how pods can communicate with other pods and with external endpoints. Both incoming and outgoing network traffic is allowed or blocked based on protocol, port, and source or destination IP addresses.
You can apply Kubernetes network policies by using kubectl commands or the Kubernetes APIs.

Calico network policies
: [Calico network policies](https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/resources/networkpolicy) are a set of the Kubernetes network policies.

Controlling traffic with network policies 

Classic clusters
Default network policies secure the public network interface of every worker node in the cluster.

You can use Calico and Kubernetes to create network policies for a cluster. With Kubernetes network policies, you can specify the network traffic that you want to allow or block to and from a pod within a cluster. To set more advanced network policies such as blocking inbound (ingress) traffic to network load balancer (NLB) services, use Calico network policies.
